basis: Renal insufficiency, thrombocytopenia and skin detachment each have HPO frequency 30-79%; detachment indicates tissue damage. Transient exanthem and isolated transaminase elevation excluded.

decisions.haematologic: involved: thrombocytopenia occurs in 30-79%, supporting intrinsic blood-cell involvement during infection.
decisions.cardiovascular: none: endothelial tropism alone does not establish clinically damaging vascular disease; annotated vasculitis occurs in only 1-4%.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: skin detachment occurs in 30-79% and represents tissue injury, beyond a transient exanthem.

basis: Axonal sensorimotor neuropathy; muscle weakness and wasting in 10/10 reflect denervation rather than direct muscle disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: distal amyotrophy in 10/10 is secondary to peripheral nerve degeneration; direct skeletal muscle pathology is not established.

basis: Inherited autoinflammatory interferonopathy. AGS is a possible presentation; the frequency of neurologic damage across this umbrella is not established.

decisions.neurologic: none: the definition identifies AGS as one possible phenotype, without establishing neurologic disease in most patients across the umbrella.

basis: Polydactyly defines disease; developmental delay 1/2, autism 2/2, structural ocular defects 1/2 and ASD 1/1 assessed. Renal agenesis 1/3 omitted by cap; very small samples.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: structural atrial septal defect is reported in 1/1 assessed; retained under the cap using the supplied frequency, with substantial sampling uncertainty.
decisions.renal: none under cap: renal agenesis 1/3 qualifies, but neurologic, ocular and cardiovascular abnormalities have higher reported frequencies.

basis: Defined by retinal capillary incompetence and dilatation with progressive central visual loss; the affected vessels fall within the cardiovascular axis.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: retinal capillary dysfunction and telangiectasia define this disease; the cardiovascular axis includes capillaries without requiring systemic involvement.

basis: Neurodegeneration and defining respiratory failure (6/6); hearing impairment 3/3 and structural joint contractures 4/4. ASD 2/6 omitted by the four-axis cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: none under cap: ASD 2/6 (~33%) qualifies, but defining respiratory failure and more frequent hearing impairment and contractures take priority.
decisions.pulmonary: primary: early respiratory failure is a defining feature explicitly named in this syndrome and documented in 6/6 assessed patients.

basis: Syndromic intellectual disability defines the umbrella; intrinsic alpha-thalassemia occurs in about 75% of the ATR-X spectrum, usually with mild hematologic effects.

decisions.haematologic: involved: intrinsic alpha-globin synthesis impairment affects approximately 75% of the ATR-X spectrum; it is a syndromic manifestation rather than an associated risk.

basis: Riboflavin deficiency is chiefly defined by stomatitis, glossitis and seborrheic skin disease. Functionally damaging corneal disease and anemia are not reliably established in >=30%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: angular stomatitis and glossitis are chief defining manifestations in the supplied definition; oral mucosa belongs to this axis.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: dyssebacia and characteristic seborrheic skin disease form part of the syndrome's defining clinical presentation.

basis: Inflammatory infiltration directly affects myocardial interstitium. The supplied definition does not establish infection, autoimmunity or a specific immune-mediated subtype.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: inflammatory cells, granulomas and occasional giant cells alone do not establish an infectious or autoimmune mechanism for this myocarditis concept.

basis: Renal cystine storage disease; corneal keratopathy commonly impairs ocular function, with crystals in 187/187. Myopathy 22/86 is <30%; rickets 2/3 is secondary to renal phosphate wasting.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: direct myopathy occurs in 22/86 (~26%); hypophosphatemic rickets 2/3 is a separately diagnosed consequence of renal phosphate wasting, not direct skeletal storage injury.
